short_definition: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure encrypts web communications using TLS/SSL.
layman_explanation: Putting web traffic inside a locked armored container so Wi-Fi snoopers cannot read your passwords.

short_definition: Registering domains using foreign alphabet characters that look identical to Latin characters.
layman_explanation: Replacing 'a' with a Cyrillic 'а' so a fake web link looks completely genuine to the naked eye.

short_definition: Injecting malicious scripts into trusted websites that execute in other users' browsers.
layman_explanation: Leaving a comment on a blog containing code that steals session cookies from anyone who reads it.

short_definition: Inserting database commands into user input fields to read or alter back-end data.
layman_explanation: Typing computer commands into a website's search box to trick it into dumping all user passwords.

short_definition: Cross-Site Request Forgery tricks authenticated users into submitting unwanted commands.
layman_explanation: Opening an image link on a forum that secretly submits a 'transfer $100' request to your bank in the background.

short_definition: An HTTP header declaring allowed source domains for browser executable content.
layman_explanation: A rulebook telling your browser: 'Only run scripts downloaded directly from our server, ignore all others.'

short_definition: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing defines permissions for browsers to fetch resources across origins.
layman_explanation: Security guidelines specifying which external websites are permitted to fetch data from your site.

short_definition: A foundational web browser security rule restricting scripts on one page from accessing another page's data.
layman_explanation: Ensuring a rogue site opened in tab B cannot read personal messages open in tab A.

short_definition: Stealing a user's session cookie to gain unauthorized access to their logged-in web account.
layman_explanation: Stealing someone's VIP ticket after they pass the gate so you can impersonate them.

short_definition: Concealing malicious elements beneath transparent overlays to trick users into clicking.
layman_explanation: Clicking a play button on a video game, but actually pressing a hidden 'Delete Account' button underneath.

short_definition: An exploit forcing a server to make HTTP requests to unintended internal or external resources.
layman_explanation: Tricking a public web server into querying secret files on its own internal private network.

short_definition: Exploiting input fields to access files outside the public web server directory.
layman_explanation: Typing '../../etc/passwd' into a web address to view protected operating system files.

short_definition: A vulnerability allowing attackers to append malicious destination URLs to untrusted redirect links.
layman_explanation: Clicking 'goodsite.com/redirect?url=evil.com' which lands you on an untrusted fishing site.

short_definition: Forcing a web application to execute or display local files stored on the server.
layman_explanation: Tricking a website into loading local system password files right on the public web page.

short_definition: Injecting external scripts into a web application to execute malicious code remotely.
layman_explanation: Tricking a server into fetching and running malware stored on a hacker's remote machine.

short_definition: Executing arbitrary shell commands on the host operating system via vulnerable input fields.
layman_explanation: Adding a semicolon and system commands into a web form field to execute terminal commands.

short_definition: Claiming an orphaned subdomain pointing to an expired external service provider.
layman_explanation: Registering a dead blog link still pointed to by 'blog.company.com' to control company content.

short_definition: Interfering with how web servers process sequences of HTTP requests received from proxies.
layman_explanation: Squeezing a hidden second request inside an order package so the server executes it unnoticed.

short_definition: Exploiting vulnerable XML parsers to read internal files or execute remote requests.
layman_explanation: Sending tampered XML document files that trick the server into revealing internal secrets.

short_definition: Manipulating resource identifiers in requests to access other users' private records.
layman_explanation: Changing your user ID in the URL from 'user/101' to 'user/102' to view someone else's profile.

short_definition: Flaws in session management allowing attackers to compromise passwords or active tokens.
layman_explanation: A web app that doesn't invalidate old session keys when users click 'Log Out'.

short_definition: Failing to implement secure settings across all layers of the web application stack.
layman_explanation: Leaving default admin passwords, test pages, or open debug logs active on a live website.

short_definition: A security appliance filtering and monitoring HTTP traffic to and from a web application.
layman_explanation: A specialized bouncer checking incoming web requests for malicious code before reaching the site.

short_definition: A header forcing browsers to interact with a website strictly over encrypted HTTPS connections.
layman_explanation: Telling a browser: 'Never attempt to connect to this site using unencrypted HTTP.'

short_definition: Forcing a victim to use a known session identifier, enabling post-login account takeover.
layman_explanation: Handing a target a pre-stamped ticket, waiting for them to validate it, then using a copy.

short_definition: Modifying parameters sent between client and server to alter application behavior.
layman_explanation: Editing a checkout form parameter from 'price=100' to 'price=1' using browser dev tools.

short_definition: Storing harmful responses in web caches to serve malicious content to subsequent visitors.
layman_explanation: Contaminating a public water fountain so everyone who drinks from it afterwards gets sick.

short_definition: An XSS attack where the vulnerability resides strictly in client-side JavaScript execution.
layman_explanation: A webpage script taking text directly from the web address bar and running it as raw code.

short_definition: An XSS attack where script payloads from the current HTTP request are reflected off the server.
layman_explanation: A search bar displaying 'You searched for: [your script]' and executing that code immediately.

short_definition: An XSS attack where malicious scripts are permanently stored on the target database.
layman_explanation: Saving a username containing executable code that runs whenever any user views your profile.

short_definition: Bypassing JSON Web Token verification by modifying header algorithm fields to 'none'.
layman_explanation: Modifying a digital badge to state 'No Signature Required' so the system skips authenticity checks.

short_definition: Exploiting script tag inclusions to leak sensitive data across different domain origins.
layman_explanation: Including another site's private script file on your page to extract user data in the background.

short_definition: Exploiting browser content-type guessing to execute malicious code masked as images.
layman_explanation: Uploading a text file disguised as a picture, which the browser misinterprets and executes as code.

short_definition: Ensuring files fetched from third-party CDNs have not been tampered with by validating hashes.
layman_explanation: Verifying a cryptographic checksum on imported library files before letting them run.

short_definition: An HTTP header controlling whether a browser can render a page inside iframe elements.
layman_explanation: Preventing malicious websites from embedding your site inside invisible frames to clickjack users.

short_definition: An HTTP header blocking browsers from MIME-sniffing responses away from declared content types.
layman_explanation: Instructing the browser: 'Treat images strictly as images, do not attempt to run them as scripts.'

short_definition: An attack targeting web software vulnerabilities for which no patch or fix currently exists.
layman_explanation: Exploiting a backdoor in popular web server software that developers haven't discovered yet.

short_definition: Exploiting framework auto-binding to overwrite sensitive object attributes during requests.
layman_explanation: Adding 'is_admin=true' to a profile update form submission to grant yourself admin access.

short_definition: Flaws in application flow design that allow users to bypass intended operational rules.
layman_explanation: Applying a $10 discount coupon 50 times in one shopping cart order because the site didn't limit uses.

short_definition: Establishing unauthorized real-time WebSocket connections using authenticated user credentials.
layman_explanation: Tricking a target browser into establishing a secret live audio/chat stream back to an attacker server.

short_definition: Injecting native template syntax into forms to execute commands inside template engines.
layman_explanation: Typing '${7*7}' into a website name field to see if the server calculates '49', indicating code execution.

short_definition: Querying enabled introspection schemas to map internal database structure and hidden fields.
layman_explanation: Asking a web API to print out its own master blueprint, exposing hidden data tables.

short_definition: Circumventing request throttling by spoofing headers or altering API endpoint paths.
layman_explanation: Adding fake client IP headers to keep submitting passwords after being blocked for too many attempts.

short_definition: Failing to validate that users possess authorization to access requested object resources.
layman_explanation: Requesting 'api/orders/999' and getting another customer's order receipt without validation.

short_definition: Failing to restrict administrative utility functions to authorized user roles.
layman_explanation: Regular users calling 'api/v1/delete_user' directly and discovering the command works.

short_definition: A denial-of-service attack targeting XML parsers using recursively expanding entity references.
layman_explanation: Sending a tiny 1KB XML file that expands in memory into gigabytes, crashing the server.

short_definition: Leaking active session identification tokens via URL query parameters or referrer logs.
layman_explanation: Putting secret session IDs inside the address bar so external sites can read them in visitor logs.

short_definition: Setting malicious cookies for a top-level domain from an untrusted subdomain.
layman_explanation: An attacker controlling 'evil.company.com' setting cookies that overwrite settings on 'company.com'.

short_definition: Inserting newline characters into user input to inject custom HTTP response headers.
layman_explanation: Adding hidden code into form inputs that forces the web server to send back altered headers.

short_definition: Injecting unescaped HTML tags into web pages to manipulate page appearance.
layman_explanation: Writing `<form>...</form>` in a comment section to render a fake login box directly on the page.

short_definition: Failing to encrypt sensitive information in transit or at rest on web applications.
layman_explanation: Transmitting credit card numbers over plain text HTTP connections visible to open Wi-Fi.

short_definition: Circumventing legacy client-side framebusting scripts to embed pages securely.
layman_explanation: Using modern browser tricks to disable old JavaScript code designed to block iframe embedding.
